# Isaac Lab 3.0 **Isaac Lab 3.0 is now generally available.** `v3.0.0` is the official Isaac Lab 3.0 release and the recommended baseline for new projects and migrations from Isaac Lab 2.x. Isaac Lab 3.0 establishes the foundation for the next generation of robot learning in Isaac Lab: one task API across multiple physics, rendering, and visualization backends; kit-less execution with Newton and OV library backends; Warp-native data paths; and unified workflows from installation through training, evaluation, and deployment. - **Newton** is a Warp-native physics backend with multiple solver paths, including MuJoCo-Warp, VBD, and MPM. It lets Isaac Lab support rigid bodies, deformables, and particles without tying tasks to one physics engine. - **OV Libraries** provide `OVPhysX` for PhysX and `OVRTX` for RTX rendering as standalone libraries. - **Isaac Sim** remains the complete path when a workflow needs the full PhysX/RTX stack, ROS bridge, XR, livestreaming, or Kit tooling, but now fully optional.

MicroDuck rendering
VBD cable insertion
MPM liquid pouring
One task API; install and run only the capabilities you need. This release targets Isaac Sim 6.2, Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.11 with CUDA 13.0, NVIDIA Warp 1.17, Newton 1.6.1, and RSL-RL 5.5.1. ## Try Isaac Lab 3.0 Install [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), clone the official release, and launch a Newton workflow: ```bash git clone --branch v3.0.0 --depth 1 https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab.git cd IsaacLab uv run isaaclab train \ --rl_library rsl_rl \ --task Isaac-Cartpole \ --viz newton_gl \ physics=newton_mjwarp ``` For standalone PhysX and RTX rendering, install the OV libraries: ```bash uv run --extra ov isaaclab train \ --rl_library rsl_rl \ --task Isaac-Cartpole-Camera \ --viz newton_gl \ physics=ovphysx \ renderer=ovrtx \ presets=rgb ``` For the complete Isaac Sim experience, including Isaac Sim PhysX, Isaac Sim RTX, ROS bridge, XR, livestreaming, and Kit tooling: ```bash uv run --extra isaacsim isaaclab train \ --rl_library rsl_rl \ --task Isaac-Cartpole \ --viz kit \ physics=isaacsim_physx ``` See the [installation guide](https://isaac-sim.github.io/IsaacLab/v3.0.0/source/isaaclab/installation.html) and [quickstart](https://isaac-sim.github.io/IsaacLab/v3.0.0/source/isaaclab/quickstart.html) for complete setup and platform-specific instructions. ## Interactive browser demos Explore Newton physics and pretrained policies directly in your browser—no installation required. Click a demo below to tune parameters, steer a robot, or inspect a policy in action.

MPM material response
Domino cascade
G1 velocity control
Franka drawer opening
**[Explore all 17 interactive demos →](https://isaac-sim.github.io/IsaacLab/v3.0.0/source/isaaclab/interactive_demos.html)** The gallery includes VBD, rigid-body, and MPM tuning; pretrained locomotion and manipulation policies; and scripted contact scenes. Each demo runs a Newton simulation locally on your CPU through WebAssembly, with camera controls, pause, and reset. ## Highlights https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b2c6481b-10da-46d3-b53e-5f9deeaae8e1 ### One environment, multiple backends Isaac Lab 3.0 introduces a factory-based, multi-backend architecture. Backend-neutral assets, sensors, scenes, and environments dispatch to the selected implementation, allowing supported tasks to change physics, rendering, or visualization without rewriting task logic. Common selectors include: ```bash physics=newton_mjwarp physics=ovphysx physics=isaacsim_physx renderer=newton_renderer renderer=ovrtx renderer=isaacsim_rtx --viz newton_gl --viz newton_rtx --viz viser --viz rerun --viz kit ``` Physics, rendering, and visualization are independent choices. A task can use Newton physics with the Newton Warp renderer while being inspected through Newton GL, Rerun, Viser, or Kit. Supported combinations remain task-specific. Inspect them with: ```bash uv run isaaclab list_envs --show_presets uv run isaaclab train --task --help ``` See [Backends and Presets](https://isaac-sim.github.io/IsaacLab/v3.0.0/source/concepts/backends_and_presets.html). ### Kit-less robot learning https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/990147ca-2277-4988-ad87-d0b5ce8cbfe3 Most Isaac Lab workflows can run without installing or launching Isaac Sim: - Newton physics with MuJoCo-Warp, VBD, MPM, coupled solvers, and the experimental Kamino solver. - Newton Warp camera rendering. - Lightweight Newton GL visualization and experimental Newton RTX visualization. - Browser-based visualization through Viser and Rerun. - OV PhysX and OV RTX through optional runtime extras. Install the full Isaac Sim stack only when a workflow requires capabilities such as Isaac Sim PhysX or RTX, ROS bridge integration, XR teleoperation, livestreaming, or Kit tooling. ### Warp-native simulation data Asset and sensor data use `ProxyArray`, providing explicit, zero-copy access to both Warp and PyTorch: ```python joint_pos_torch = robot.data.joint_pos.torch joint_pos_warp = robot.data.joint_pos.warp ``` Structured Warp data, fused GPU kernels, lazy buffers, cached views, and CUDA graph support reduce Python and tensor-conversion overhead while preserving PyTorch interoperability. ### Unified training and playback commands The `isaaclab` command provides one workflow across supported RL libraries and backends: ```bash uv run isaaclab train --rl_library rsl_rl --task Isaac-Cartpole uv run isaaclab play --rl_library rsl_rl --task Isaac-Cartpole --checkpoint latest ``` Isaac Lab 3.0 integrates: - RSL-RL - RL-Games - skrl with PyTorch or JAX - Stable-Baselines3 - RLinf - TorchRL Checkpoint selection is standardized around `--checkpoint`, including `latest`, `best`, `pretrained`, and explicit paths. See [Reinforcement Learning](https://isaac-sim.github.io/IsaacLab/v3.0.0/source/concepts/reinforcement_learning.html). ### Improved simulation functionalities https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fea5137a-0243-40a5-97d2-5a6fcb3af055 Isaac Lab 3.0 adds and expands: - Backend-neutral sensors for frame-transformer, IMU/PVA, joint-wrench, and ray-caster workflows. - Explicit total, normal, friction, filtered, and aggregate contact-force contracts. - Warp-native ray casting. - Surface and volume deformables with composable schema fragments. - Newton VBD and rigid/deformable/MPM coupling. - Backend-neutral visual materials and material randomization. - Modular combinations between physics, renderer, and visualizers. ### From simulation to deployment Isaac Lab 3.0 strengthens the complete robot-learning workflow with: - Isaac Capture integration through `isaaclab_teleop`, including pipeline-based retargeting, CloudXR, and MCAP record/replay. - LEAPP policy export and deployment, including camera and deformable inputs. - Bidirectional PhysX↔Newton policy-transfer guidance and validated examples. See [Transfer Policies Between PhysX and Newton](https://isaac-sim.github.io/IsaacLab/v3.0.0/source/how-to/transfer_policies_between_physx_and_newton.html). ### A better developer experience Isaac Lab 3.0 simplifies common development workflows: - `uv run` creates and synchronizes the project environment automatically. - Isaac Lab can be installed as a Python dependency in downstream projects. - The installed CLI discovers downstream task packages through entry points. - The environment browser exposes tasks, presets, supported RL libraries, and launch commands. - Packaged examples are available through `isaaclab demo` and `isaaclab example`. - Repository-owned agent skills guide installation, migration, environment creation, backend selection, training, debugging, asset preparation, and policy transfer. ## Changes since Early Access ### Updated dependencies The GA release updates the core dependency versions from EA: - Isaac Sim 6.1 → **6.2** - NVIDIA Warp 1.16 → **1.17** - Newton 1.5.2 → **1.6.1** - RSL-RL 5.4.1 → **5.5.1** - Kit-less OpenUSD 25.05 → **26.08** through `usd-exchange` 3.0.1 - OVRTX → **0.5.1** - OVStage → **0.2.1** - OVPhysX → **0.6.4** ### Runtime and platform stabilization Since EA, Isaac Lab has received broad stabilization across: - Isaac Sim 6.2 installation, assets, importers, containers, and China-region storage. - Windows wheel installation and Newton CUDA graph initialization. - Linux aarch64 and DGX Spark launch behavior. - RTX multi-GPU training with PyTorch 2.11 and CUDA 13. - Ctrl+C and shutdown handling across Kit and standalone visualizers. - Monitor-free and virtual-display Newton visualization. - OVRTX buffer lifetime, stream ordering, cloning, and multi-camera rendering. - Newton camera poses, HDR backgrounds, distortion handling, and RTX markers. - PhysX, OVPhysX, and Newton contact-force behavior. ### Learning and environment improvements GA adds and improves: - TorchRL integration and PPO examples. - A dedicated `skrl-jax` extra. - RSL-RL mixed-precision and `torch.compile` options. - Automatic Weights & Biases checkpoint resolution. - Video capture for zero and random agents. - Time-ordered observation histories and configurable observation delay. - Improved task and RL-library compatibility reporting. - Camera inputs and frame history for LEAPP. - Additional deformable, particle, cable, and coupled-solver examples. - Interactive demo and example selection in Newton GL.
Upgrading from Isaac Lab 3.0 Early Access to 3.0 GA ### Application launching `AppLauncher` now provides only limited compatibility. New and migrated scripts should use `launch_simulation`: ```python from isaaclab.app import launch_simulation env_cfg = MyEnvCfg() with launch_simulation(env_cfg, args_cli): env = MyEnv(env_cfg) env.reset() while env.sim.is_running(): env.step(actions) ``` The following removed or changed APIs require attention in custom scripts: - `AppLauncher.is_available` - `AppLauncher.has_gui` - `AppLauncher.has_window` - `AppLauncher.device` - `SimulationContext.is_headless_or_exist_active_visualizer` - `SettingsManager.instance()` - `SettingsManager.set_bool`, `set_int`, `set_float`, and `set_string` - `isaaclab.app.make_physics_cfg` - `isaaclab.sim.utils.update_stage` - `isaaclab.sim.utils.show_stage_in_viewport` - The hidden `--cpu` argument; use `--device cpu` Use `SimulationContext.is_running()`, `get_settings_manager()`, `SettingsManager.set()`, and configuration-driven backend selection instead. ### Programmatic task configuration The old Hydra decorator and override helpers were removed. Replace `hydra_task_config`, `parse_overrides`, and `apply_overrides` with: ```python from isaaclab_tasks.utils import resolve_task_config env_cfg, agent_cfg = resolve_task_config( task_name, "rsl_rl_cfg_entry_point", play_mode=False, overrides=[ "physics=newton_mjwarp", "env.scene.num_envs=128", ], ) ``` Pass the resolved environment and agent configurations directly to the environment or training entrypoint. ### Direct environment configuration Maintained Direct tasks now declare assets and sensors under `cfg.scene`. Update paths such as: ```python # EA cfg.robot_cfg cfg.tiled_camera ``` to: ```python # GA cfg.scene.robot cfg.scene.tiled_camera ``` Custom `_setup_scene()` implementations copied from maintained tasks should be reviewed against the GA implementation. Reorientation environments using asymmetric observations must explicitly declare their joint-wrench sensor under `cfg.scene`. ### Physics schema fragments Maintained task and asset configurations now use composable schema fragments rather than combined property configurations. Legacy combined configurations remain available as deprecated aliases in 3.0, but code that mutates the structure of shipped configurations may break because spawner slots now commonly contain fragment lists. Replace: ```python import isaaclab.sim as sim_utils rigid_props = sim_utils.RigidBodyPropertiesCfg( kinematic_enabled=False, linear_damping=0.1, ) ``` with: ```python from isaaclab.sim.schemas import UsdPhysicsRigidBodyCfg from isaaclab_physx.sim.schemas import PhysxRigidBodyCfg rigid_props = [ UsdPhysicsRigidBodyCfg(kinematic_enabled=False), PhysxRigidBodyCfg(linear_damping=0.1), ] ``` Users modifying shipped assets must select the fragment that owns the field rather than assuming the slot is one object. Three non-USD settings moved onto the spawner configuration: - `fix_root_link` - `ensure_drives_exist` - `mesh_collision_props` The legacy `define_*` and `modify_*` schema writers are deprecated in favor of expression-targeted `apply_*` writers. ### Manager term entity selections Resolved `SceneEntityCfg` selections may now be device tensors or slices instead of host lists. Custom observation, reward, event, curriculum, and termination terms should preserve the selected dimension: ```python # Fragile with a device-resident selection value = data[:, cfg.body_ids[0]] # GA-compatible value = data[:, cfg.body_ids][:, 0] ``` Replace patterns such as: ```python torch.tensor(cfg.body_ids) isinstance(cfg.body_ids, list) ``` with direct use of the resolved tensor or an explicit slice check. Class-based terms may still see host selections during `__init__`, but term calls receive finalized selections. ### Environment reset selectors `ManagerBasedEnv.reset()` accepts `env_ids` as its first positional argument. `reset_to(state, env_ids=...)` accepts the selector after state. Pass Gymnasium seed and options to `reset()` by keyword: ```python env.reset(env_ids) env.reset(seed=42) ``` Custom reset callbacks must accept both slices and device indices: ```python def reset(self, env_ids: slice | torch.Tensor): selected_state = self.state[env_ids] batch_size = selected_state.shape[0] ``` Avoid assuming the selector supports: ```python len(env_ids) env_ids.tolist() ``` When only the selected batch size is needed, derive it from selected data or from the slice bounds. ### Observation noise callbacks The observation manager no longer creates a defensive copy before calling configured noise functions. In-place noise can now modify a shared source tensor and corrupt other observations. Replace: ```python def add_bias(data, bias): return data.add_(bias) ``` with: ```python def add_bias(data, bias): return data + bias ``` If in-place operations are required, clone first: ```python return data.clone().add_(bias) ``` Users with custom `NoiseCfg` or `NoiseModelCfg` implementations should audit every callback. ### Logging values Several manager and task metrics now report zero-dimensional device tensors instead of Python floats to avoid GPU synchronization. Code that formats, serializes, or compares these values as Python numbers should convert explicitly: ```python success_rate = float(extras["log"]["Metrics/success_rate"]) # or success_rate = extras["log"]["Metrics/success_rate"].item() ``` ### Camera observations The generic `isaaclab.envs.mdp.image` term was removed. Use modality-specific terms: - `image_rgb` - `image_depth` - `image_normals` - `image_segmentation` Also: - Replace `permute=True` with `channel_first=True`. - Remove the old `clone` option. - Configure `frame_stack` on the image term. - Expect `image_rgb` to drop the alpha channel. For example: ```python policy_image = ObsTerm( func=mdp.image_rgb, params={ "sensor_cfg": SceneEntityCfg("camera"), "channel_first": True, "frame_stack": 4, }, ) ``` Vision-policy users should validate observation shapes, channel order, normalization, and frame history before loading an EA checkpoint. ### Visualizer configuration Renderer selection now takes a configuration object rather than a nickname: ```python # EA cfg.streaming_cam_renderer = "ovrtx" ``` ```python # GA from isaaclab_ov.renderers import OVRTXRendererCfg cfg.streaming_cam_renderer_cfg = OVRTXRendererCfg() ``` The tiled-camera fields move to the unified streaming-camera API: | EA field | GA field | |---|---| | `tiled_cam_view` | `streaming_view` | | `tiled_cam_num` | `streaming_envs` | | `tiled_cam_prim_path` | `streaming_sensor_prim_path` | | `tiled_cam_eye` | `streaming_cam_eye` | | `tiled_cam_renderer` | `streaming_cam_renderer_cfg` | `NewtonVisualizerCfg` is replaced by `NewtonGLVisualizerCfg` or `NewtonRTXVisualizerCfg`. The CLI alias `--viz newton` remains deprecated; use: ```bash --viz newton_gl ``` Code inspecting parsed visualizer arguments must now distinguish: ```python args_cli.visualizer is None # --viz was omitted args_cli.visualizer == [] # --viz none was passed ``` ### Video recording `gym.wrappers.RecordVideo` is no longer the supported recording path. Configure recorders through the environment: ```python from isaaclab.envs.utils.video_recorder_cfg import VideoRecorderCfg env_cfg.video_recorders = [ VideoRecorderCfg( source="visualizer", output_dir="videos/", video_length=200, ) ] ``` Viewport position should be configured through `SimulationCfg.default_visualizer_cfg`, not through `VideoRecorderCfg`. ### Stable-Baselines3 action bounds `Sb3VecEnvWrapper` now exposes normalized `[-1, 1]` bounds for otherwise unbounded continuous action spaces instead of the EA fallback of `[-100, 100]`. To preserve the EA action space while loading an existing checkpoint: ```python Sb3VecEnvWrapper(env, action_bounds=(-100, 100)) ``` New training should generally use the GA default bounds. ### TorchScript loading `load_torchscript_model` now raises `RuntimeError` when loading fails instead of returning `None`. Replace: ```python model = load_torchscript_model(path) if model is None: ... ``` with: ```python try: model = load_torchscript_model(path) except RuntimeError: ... ```
Migrating from Isaac Lab 2.x Isaac Lab 3.0 is a major release. Downstream 2.x projects should review the complete [Isaac Lab 2.x → 3.0 migration guide](https://isaac-sim.github.io/IsaacLab/v3.0.0/source/isaaclab/migrating.html). The most important migration areas are summarized below. ### Installation Start from a fresh Python 3.12 environment instead of upgrading a 2.x environment in place. Use: ```bash uv run isaaclab ... ``` Add optional runtimes before `isaaclab`: ```bash uv run --extra isaacsim isaaclab ... uv run --extra ov isaaclab ... ``` ### Backend configuration Keep core asset imports backend-neutral and move backend-owned configuration into `isaaclab_physx`, `isaaclab_newton`, or `isaaclab_ov`. Use `PresetCfg` and typed selectors: ```bash physics=newton_mjwarp physics=isaacsim_physx renderer=newton_renderer renderer=ovrtx presets=rgb ``` ### Quaternion order All Isaac Lab quaternion APIs, configuration values, asset data, sensor data, and math utilities now use: ```text Isaac Lab 2.x: (w, x, y, z) Isaac Lab 3.0: (x, y, z, w) ``` The identity quaternion changes from: ```text (1, 0, 0, 0) ``` to: ```text (0, 0, 0, 1) ``` Review hard-coded rotations, reset states, goals, controller targets, observations, and custom math. ### ProxyArray data access Asset and sensor `.data.*` properties return `ProxyArray`. Use `.torch` or `.warp` explicitly: ```python root_pos = robot.data.root_pos_w.torch joint_pos = robot.data.joint_pos.torch joint_pos_warp = robot.data.joint_pos.warp ``` Replace patterns such as: ```python robot.data.root_pos_w.clone() torch.zeros_like(robot.data.joint_pos) ``` with: ```python robot.data.root_pos_w.torch.clone() torch.zeros_like(robot.data.joint_pos.torch) ``` ### Indexed and masked writes Migrate ambiguous asset writes to explicit index or mask variants: ```python robot.write_root_pose_to_sim_index( root_pose=partial_pose, env_ids=env_ids, ) robot.write_root_pose_to_sim_mask( root_pose=full_pose, env_mask=env_mask, ) ``` Index variants accept partial data for selected environments. Mask variants accept full data for all environments plus a Boolean mask. ### Actuator ownership Actuator commands and telemetry now live under `robot.actuators`: ```python robot.actuators.target_command.set_effort_index( value=efforts, joint_ids=joint_ids, ) applied_effort = robot.actuators.applied_effort.torch ``` Actuator setters are keyword-only. Canonical limit names distinguish rated actuator limits from solver-enforced joint limits: - `effort_limit` → `actuator_effort_limit` - `effort_limit_sim` → `joint_effort_limit` - `velocity_limit_sim` → `joint_velocity_limit` Explicit actuator groups now preserve authored solver effort limits instead of automatically raising them. Review clipping behavior for policies that relied only on actuator-model limits. ### Sensor contracts - The 2.x full-state `IMU` is now `PVA`. - The new `IMU` reports angular velocity and linear acceleration. - Use `JointWrenchSensor` instead of `ArticulationData.body_incoming_joint_wrench_b`. - Use `FrameTransformer` instead of contact-sensor pose properties. - Prefer explicit total, normal, friction, aggregate, and filtered contact-force properties. ### Asset and view naming - `XformPrimView` → `FrameView` - `root_physx_view` → backend-specific `root_view` - `RigidObjectCollection.object_*` → `body_*` - The former soft-body model is replaced by explicit surface and volume deformable APIs. Several old names remain as deprecated aliases, but new code should use the GA names. ### Training and checkpoints Backend-local and RL-library-local `train.py` and `play.py` entrypoints were removed. Use: ```bash uv run isaaclab train --rl_library rsl_rl --task Isaac-Cartpole uv run isaaclab play --rl_library rsl_rl --task Isaac-Cartpole --checkpoint latest ``` Resume and playback workflows consistently use `--checkpoint`. ### Visualization and recording - Use `--viz` to select visualizers. - `--headless` no longer disables configured visualizers. - Use `--viz none` to disable all visualizers. - Move viewport configuration from `env_cfg.viewer` to `SimulationCfg`. - Use `VideoRecorderCfg` instead of `gym.wrappers.RecordVideo`. ### Direct Isaac Sim imports Isaac Lab no longer preloads extensions only to make their Python modules importable. If downstream code must import an Isaac Sim extension directly, enable it after Kit starts: ```python from isaaclab.sim.utils import enable_extension enable_extension("isaacsim.core.experimental.prims") ``` Prefer an Isaac Lab API where one is available. Do not import `enable_extension` from `isaacsim.core.experimental.utils.app`, because that module may not be importable until its extension is already enabled. ### URDF and MJCF importers The rewritten importers change output layout and remove or deprecate several options: - URDF output filenames are determined automatically. - `make_instanceable` is no longer supported; output is instanceable by default. - MJCF fixedness, density, inertia, and site import are inferred from the model. - MJCF-imported USDs use nested rigid bodies. - Generated assets support multiple physics backends. Review custom conversion scripts and code that traverses generated USD hierarchies. ### Teleoperation The native `isaaclab.devices.openxr` stack is deprecated. Use Isaac Capture through: - `isaaclab_teleop` - `IsaacTeleopDevice` - `IsaacTeleopCfg` - Pipeline-based retargeters
## Get help The comprehensive [Isaac Lab 2.x → 3.0 migration guide](https://isaac-sim.github.io/IsaacLab/v3.0.0/source/isaaclab/migrating.html) covers installation, package moves, API mappings, quaternions, `ProxyArray`, actuators, sensors, visualizers, recording, RL commands, importers, benchmarks, teleoperation, and deformables. Isaac Lab also ships repository-owned agent skills that route coding agents through current documentation, source APIs, examples, and focused validation commands. For example, ask your coding agent to: - “Use `isaaclab-migrating-2x-to-3x` to migrate this project.” - “Use `isaaclab-selecting-backends` to determine which backends this task supports.” - “Use `isaaclab-preparing-assets-for-newton` to validate this robot for MJWarp.” - “Use `isaaclab-transferring-policies-sim-to-sim` to evaluate this checkpoint in PhysX and Newton.” - “Use `isaaclab-setup-troubleshooting` to diagnose this installation.” - “Use `isaaclab-migrating-from-isaac-gym` to migrate a project from Isaac Gym.” Report reproducible bugs through [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/issues), ask questions in [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/discussions), and join the [NVIDIA Omniverse Discord](https://discord.gg/nvidiaomniverse). Thank you to every contributor and Early Access user who tested migrations, reported regressions, and helped bring Isaac Lab 3.0 to General Availability. We are excited to see what you build with the official release. [Full changes since Early Access](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/compare/v3.0.0-EA...v3.0.0)

Prebuilt Newton WebAssembly simulations, their browser viewer, and exporter source for Isaac Lab documentation.

The documentation stages one reviewed, commit-named archive and verifies its SHA-256. This release is the permanent bundle container; updates add assets here without creating a new numbered release. Existing assets remain available for reproducible builds.

[Documentation update PR #8559](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/pull/8559) · [Review the gallery](https://maxkra15.github.io/isaaclab-browser-demos/lab/?v=grains-v1)

## Preview a bundle

Download the archive selected by `.github/actions/_lib/stage-browser-demos.sh`, extract it, and enter its top-level directory. Then run:

```bash
python -m http.server 8000 --directory site
```

Open `http://localhost:8000/interactive/`. The archive includes `exporters/`, scene and rebuild instructions, licenses, and `tools/publish.py`. Running the demos needs only a browser. Rebuilding physics requires the pinned internal Newton Web compiler and Emscripten.

## Publish an update

Reuse the `interactive-releases` publishing branch. Commit the reviewed site, create a commit-named archive and checksum, and upload both to this same release. Update the archive URL and SHA-256 together in the docs PR. Keep earlier assets and compatibility directories.

The current publishing branch is [available in the contributor fork](https://github.com/maxkra15/IsaacLab/tree/interactive-releases). Creating it in the official repository requires an administrator under the repository's branch-creation rule. Runtime bundles are hosted in this official release and served by Isaac Lab documentation.

# Isaac Lab 3.0 Early Access

**Isaac Lab 3.0 Early Access is ready.**

Isaac Lab 3.0 establishes the foundation for the next generation of robot learning in Isaac Lab: one task API across multiple physics, rendering, and visualization backends; kit-less execution; Warp-native data paths; and unified workflows from installation through training, evaluation, and deployment.

This release is built for **Isaac Sim 6.1**, Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.11, NVIDIA Warp 1.16, and Newton 1.5.2.

> [!NOTE]
> **Early Access status**
>
> The architecture and feature set for Isaac Lab 3.0 are ready for users to build on. From Early Access to General Availability, the `release/3.0.0` branch will focus only on bug fixes, stability, compatibility, and documentation improvements. General Availability is targeted toward the end of October 2026.
>
> We encourage you to start migrating, training, and testing now—and to tell us what you find.

## Try Isaac Lab 3.0 today

Install [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), clone the Early Access branch, and launch a kit-less Newton workflow:

```bash
git clone --branch release/3.0.0 https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab.git
cd IsaacLab

uv run isaaclab train \
    --rl_library rsl_rl \
    --task Isaac-Cartpole \
    physics=newton_mjwarp \
    --viz newton_gl
```

For a fully kit-less PhysX and RTX rendering workflow, use OVPhysX and OVRTX backends. The `ov` extra installs both optional runtimes; Isaac Sim is not installed or launched:

```bash
uv run --extra ov isaaclab train \
    --rl_library rsl_rl \
    --task Isaac-Cartpole-Camera-Direct \
    physics=ovphysx \
    renderer=ovrtx \
    presets=rgb \
    --viz newton_gl
```

For the full Isaac Sim experience with Isaac Sim PhysX, Isaac Sim RTX rendering, Isaac Sim ROS bridge, and other Kit integrations:

```bash
uv run --extra isaacsim isaaclab train \
    --rl_library rsl_rl \
    --task Isaac-Cartpole \
    physics=isaacsim_physx \
    --viz kit
```

See the [Isaac Lab 3.0 installation guide](https://isaac-sim.github.io/IsaacLab/release/3.0.0/source/setup/installation/index.html) and [quickstart](https://isaac-sim.github.io/IsaacLab/release/3.0.0/source/setup/quickstart.html) for the complete setup options.

## Highlights

### One environment, multiple backends

Isaac Lab 3.0 introduces a factory-based, multi-backend architecture. Common asset, sensor, and scene APIs dispatch to the selected implementation, allowing supported tasks to change physics, rendering, or visualization without rewriting the environment.

Use tested configuration selectors at launch:

```bash
physics=isaacsim_physx
physics=ovphysx
physics=newton_mjwarp

renderer=isaacsim_rtx
renderer=ovrtx
renderer=newton_renderer

--viz newton_gl
--viz newton_rtx
--viz viser
--viz rerun
--viz kit
```

Physics, rendering, and visualization are now separate choices. A task can use Newton physics with the Newton Warp renderer, for example, while being inspected through Newton GL, Rerun, or Viser. Supported combinations remain task-specific and are reported through each task’s `--help` output. See [Backends and Presets](https://isaac-sim.github.io/IsaacLab/release/3.0.0/source/concepts/backends_and_presets.html).

### Kit-less robot learning

Many Isaac Lab workflows can now run without installing or launching Isaac Sim:

- Newton physics with multi-solver capabilities - MuJoCo-Warp, VBD, MPM and coupled-solver workflows, with expanded support for deformables, cables, and particle systems.
- Experimental Kamino solver for complex articulations.
- Newton Warp camera rendering.
- Lightweight Newton GL visualization, as well as experimental Newton RTX visualization.
- Browser-based visualization through Viser and Rerun.
- OV PhysX and OV RTX through optional runtime extras.

Install the full Isaac Sim stack only when a workflow needs capabilities such as XR teleoperation, Isaac Sim PhysX, Isaac Sim RTX, Isaac Sim ROS bridge, livestreaming, or Kit tooling.

### Warp-native simulation data

Asset and sensor data now use `ProxyArray`, providing explicit, zero-copy access to both Warp and PyTorch:

```python
joint_pos_torch = robot.data.joint_pos.torch
joint_pos_warp = robot.data.joint_pos.warp
```

Structured Warp data, fused GPU kernels, cached views, and CUDA graph support reduce Python and tensor-conversion overhead while keeping PyTorch interoperability straightforward.

### Unified training, playback, and benchmarking

The new `isaaclab` command replaces library-specific workflow scripts:

```bash
uv run isaaclab train --rl_library rsl_rl --task Isaac-Cartpole
uv run isaaclab play --rl_library rsl_rl --task Isaac-Cartpole --checkpoint latest
uv run isaaclab benchmark runtime --task Isaac-Cartpole
```

Isaac Lab provides unified integration for:

- RSL-RL (installed by default)
- skrl
- RL-Games
- Stable-Baselines3
- RLinf for VLA post-training

Checkpoint selection is standardized around `--checkpoint`, including `latest`, `best`, `pretrained`, and explicit paths. The benchmark system now covers startup, runtime, training, playback, and multi-GPU workflows through one typed API. See [Reinforcement Learning](https://isaac-sim.github.io/IsaacLab/release/3.0.0/source/concepts/reinforcement_learning.html).

### Pluggable visualization and recording

Isaac Lab 3.0 includes five visualizers:

- **Newton GL** for lightweight local inspection and physics debugging.
- **Newton RTX** for high-quality kit-less rendering.
- **Kit** for the complete Isaac Sim and USD experience.
- **Viser** for browser-based visualization and sharing.
- **Rerun** for web viewing, recording, and timeline replay.

Visualizers can be selected with `--viz`:

```bash
uv run --extra rerun isaaclab play \
    --task Isaac-Cartpole \
    --checkpoint latest \
    --viz newton_gl
```

Recording is now configuration-owned and can capture a visualizer, a tiled view, or a scene camera. Camera pipelines also gain HDR output and the renderer-neutral PPISP image-signal-processing pipeline. See [Visualization](https://isaac-sim.github.io/IsaacLab/release/3.0.0/source/concepts/visualization.html).

### Stronger sensors, deformables, and simulation contracts

Isaac Lab 3.0 adds/expands:

- Backend-neutral contact, frame-transformer, IMU/PVA, joint-wrench, and ray-caster workflows.
- Explicit normal, friction, filtered, and aggregate contact-force contracts.
- A Warp-native ray-casting pipeline.
- Surface and volume deformables with backend-specific implementations.
- Newton VBD and rigid/deformable/MPM coupling.
- Backend-neutral visual materials and material randomization.
- Deterministic physics requests translated by each supported backend.

### From simulation to deployment

Isaac Lab 3.0 strengthens the complete robot-learning workflow:

- Isaac Teleop integration with pipeline-based retargeting, CloudXR, and MCAP record/replay.
- Isaac Lab Mimic and SkillGen demonstration-generation workflows.
- Visually augmented imitation learning.
- Multi-GPU and multi-node RL training.
- LEAPP policy export and deployment commands.
- Bidirectional PhysX↔Newton policy-transfer guidance and validated examples for Franka Lift, G1 rough locomotion, and ANYmal-D rough locomotion.

See [Transfer Policies Between PhysX and Newton](https://isaac-sim.github.io/IsaacLab/release/3.0.0/source/how-to/transfer_policies_between_physx_and_newton.html).

### A better developer experience

Isaac Lab 3.0 makes the common path much simpler:

- `uv run` creates and synchronizes the project environment automatically.
- Isaac Lab can be installed as a Python dependency in downstream projects.
- The installed CLI discovers downstream task packages through entry points.
- The environment browser exposes task presets and builds launch commands interactively.
- The performance dashboard compares backends and tracks regressions.
- The repository ships **17 user-facing agent skills** for installation, migration, environment creation, backend selection, Newton asset preparation, training, debugging, sim-to-sim transfer, sensors, actuators, and more.

## Core breaking changes

Isaac Lab 3.0 is a major release. Compatibility shims remain for several renamed APIs, but downstream projects should migrate now rather than depending on those shims.

### Installation and runtime

- Start from a fresh Python 3.12 environment; do not upgrade a 2.x environment in place.
- Full Isaac Sim workflows require Isaac Sim 6.1.
- `uv run` is now the recommended workflow; `isaaclab.sh` is deprecated and will be removed in a future release.
- Optional integrations are selected through extras such as `isaacsim`, `ovphysx`, `ovrtx`, `teleop`, `mimic`, and individual RL libraries.

### Quaternions changed from WXYZ to XYZW

All Isaac Lab quaternion APIs, configuration values, asset and sensor data, and math utilities now use:

```text
Isaac Lab 2.x: (w, x, y, z)
Isaac Lab 3.0: (x, y, z, w)
```

The identity quaternion therefore changes from `(1, 0, 0, 0)` to `(0, 0, 0, 1)`.

Review hard-coded asset rotations, reset states, goals, controller targets, observations, and custom math. The migration guide includes a source scanner and a runtime detector for quaternion-bearing `ProxyArray.torch` accesses.

### Data properties now return `ProxyArray`

Asset and sensor `.data.*` properties no longer return a `torch.Tensor` directly. Use `.torch` or `.warp` explicitly:

```python
root_pos = robot.data.root_pos_w.torch
```

Temporary Torch interoperability remains available for some operations but emits deprecation warnings.

### Write methods distinguish indices from masks

The ambiguous `write_*_to_sim(data, env_ids)` methods were removed. Use:

```python
robot.write_root_pose_to_sim_index(root_pose=pose, env_ids=env_ids)
robot.write_root_pose_to_sim_mask(root_pose=pose, env_mask=env_mask)
```

This convention applies across rigid objects, articulations, rigid-object collections, and joint-property writers.

### Backend configuration is explicit

Solver-common schema configuration lives under `isaaclab.sim.schemas`; PhysX- and Newton-specific configuration lives under `isaaclab_physx` and `isaaclab_newton`.

Core asset imports such as `Articulation` remain backend-neutral, while backend-owned APIs such as `SurfaceGripper` move to their backend package. Multi-backend tasks should use `PresetCfg` and typed `physics=` / `renderer=` selectors.

Custom scripts that load registered task configuration should use the shared task-composition helpers rather than passing unresolved configuration classes directly to an environment.

### Actuator ownership moved to `ActuatorCollection`

Actuator commands and telemetry now live under `robot.actuators`:

```python
robot.actuators.target_command.set_effort_index(
    value=efforts,
    joint_ids=joint_ids,
)
applied = robot.actuators.applied_effort.torch
```

Actuator setters are keyword-only. Canonical limit names now distinguish the actuator’s rated limits from solver-enforced joint limits:

- `effort_limit` → `actuator_effort_limit`
- `effort_limit_sim` → `joint_effort_limit`
- `velocity_limit_sim` → `joint_velocity_limit`

Explicit actuator groups now preserve authored solver effort limits instead of automatically raising them, which can change clipping behavior.

### Sensor contracts changed

- The 2.x full-state `IMU` is now `PVA`.
- The new `IMU` reports only angular velocity and linear acceleration.
- `ArticulationData.body_incoming_joint_wrench_b` was removed; configure a `JointWrenchSensor`.
- Contact-force properties now distinguish total, normal, friction, aggregate, and filtered forces.
- Contact-sensor pose properties are deprecated; use `FrameTransformer`.

### Asset and view naming changed

- `XformPrimView` → `FrameView`
- `root_physx_view` → backend-specific `root_view`
- `RigidObjectCollection.object_*` → `body_*`
- The former soft-body model is replaced by explicit surface and volume deformable APIs.

Several old names remain as deprecated aliases through the 3.x line.

### Training and checkpoint commands changed

Backend-local and RL-library-local `train.py` and `play.py` entrypoints were removed. Use `isaaclab train` and `isaaclab play` with `--rl_library`.

Resume and playback workflows now consistently use `--checkpoint`.

### Visualization and recording changed

- `--viz` selects visualizers.
- `--headless` is removed and no longer disables configured visualizers.
- Use `--viz none` to explicitly disable all visualizers.
- Viewport configuration moved from `env_cfg.viewer` to `SimulationCfg` visualizer configuration.
- `gym.wrappers.RecordVideo` is no longer supported; use `VideoRecorderCfg`.

### Direct Isaac Sim imports require attention

Isaac Lab no longer preloads extensions simply to make their Python modules importable. Downstream projects that import Isaac Sim extensions directly must enable them after the Kit application starts:

```python
from isaaclab.sim.utils import enable_extension

enable_extension("isaacsim.core.experimental.prims")
```

Legacy `isaacsim.core.*` and `isaacsim.sensors.*` imports should be replaced with Isaac Lab APIs where available or the corresponding Isaac Sim experimental APIs.

### URDF and MJCF importers were rewritten

The new importer pipelines change output layout and remove/deprecate several options:

- URDF output filenames are determined automatically.
- `make_instanceable` is no longer supported; output is instanceable by default.
- MJCF fixedness, density, inertia, and site import are inferred from the model.
- MJCF-imported USDs now use nested rigid bodies.

URDF and MJCF importers now generate multi-backend physics enabled assets with nested rigid bodies.
Review custom conversion scripts and code that traverses generated USD hierarchies.

### Teleoperation moved to Isaac Teleop

The native `isaaclab.devices.openxr` stack is deprecated. Use `isaaclab_teleop`, `IsaacTeleopDevice`, `IsaacTeleopCfg`, and Isaac Teleop’s pipeline-based retargeters.

### Benchmark entrypoints were consolidated

Legacy benchmark scripts and wrapper shell scripts were replaced by:

```bash
isaaclab benchmark runtime
isaaclab benchmark startup
isaaclab benchmark training
isaaclab benchmark play
```

The public benchmark API moved from `isaaclab.test.benchmark` to `isaaclab.benchmark`.

## Migration help

The comprehensive [Isaac Lab 2.x → 3.0 migration guide](https://isaac-sim.github.io/IsaacLab/release/3.0.0/source/migration/migrating_to_isaaclab_3-0.html) covers installation, package moves, API mappings, quaternions, `ProxyArray`, actuators, sensors, visualizers, recording, RL commands, importers, benchmarks, teleoperation, and deformables.

Isaac Lab also ships repository-owned [agent skills](https://isaac-sim.github.io/IsaacLab/release/3.0.0/source/developer-tools/agent_skills.html), discovered automatically by Codex and Claude. For example, ask your coding agent to:

- “Use `isaaclab-migrating-2x-to-3x` to migrate this project.”
- “Use `isaaclab-selecting-backends` to determine which backends this task supports.”
- “Use `isaaclab-preparing-assets-for-newton` to validate this robot for MJWarp.”
- “Use `isaaclab-transferring-policies-sim-to-sim` to evaluate this checkpoint in PhysX and Newton.”
- “Use `isaaclab-setup-troubleshooting` to diagnose this installation.”
- "Use `isaaclab-migrating-from-isaac-gym` to migrate a project from Isaac Gym."

These skills route the agent through the current documentation, APIs, examples, and focused validation commands instead of relying on remembered 2.x patterns.

## Known limitations

Backend and preset support remains task-specific. Important limitations include:

- Surface-gripper tasks require CPU simulation with `physics=isaacsim_physx`.
- Pink IK tasks are supported on Linux x86_64 and aarch64; their dependencies are not available through the Windows installation.
- Closed-loop Digit articulations remain PhysX-only.
- Isaac Sim backends cannot be combined with OVPhysX and OVRTX.

Review the current [Known Issues](https://isaac-sim.github.io/IsaacLab/release/3.0.0/source/refs/issues.html) for more details.

## Help us finish 3.0

Early Access is the best time to exercise your real projects:

- Migrate a 2.x task.
- Try the same environment in PhysX and Newton.
- Test your checkpoints with the unified `play` workflow.
- Exercise Windows, aarch64, Docker, and multi-GPU setups.
- Try the migration and troubleshooting agent skills.
- Share demonstrations and performance results.

Report reproducible bugs through [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/issues), ask questions in [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/discussions), and join the [NVIDIA Omniverse Discord](https://discord.gg/nvidiaomniverse).

Thank you to every contributor and early adopter who helped reshape Isaac Lab for 3.0. We are excited to see what you build.
